title: Write the best X thread explaining $OFFR
description:
$OFFR (Offline Research) is a 35B AI that runs on your phone with zero internet: cited answers, no wifi, no cloud, no API.

We're looking for the clearest X thread explaining what OFFR is and how it works, in your own words.

WHAT TO DO
Post a thread on X (at least 5 posts) that explains:
1. What OFFR is and the problem it solves
2. How it works (running offline, citations, the 35B model)
3. Who it's useful for
4. Any honest limits (for example, the benchmark results come from a small test set)

REQUIRED IN THE THREAD
- this tweet should be quoted : https://x.com/RealShark77/status/2116888075980976457?a=MpoKGjGjMnrpVNVaBM4&s=20
- Mention the project: @OFFR54
- Mention the creator: @RealShark77
- Include the token contract address (Base): 0xee9069e8f520652e59674fad2120f6dea2671ba3
- Disclose that you're taking part in a bounty (for example, "#bounty" or "entered in a poidh bounty")

HOW TO CLAIM
Submit one claim on poidh with:
- A screenshot of the first post of your thread as the proof image
- A link to the thread
- Your X handle in the description

RULES
- Original work only. Copy-pasted or AI-spam threads will be rejected.
- Be accurate. No price predictions, no promises of returns, and no claims that OFFR beats other AI models.
- One claim per person.
- Deadline: 15-11-2026

JUDGING
The creator will pick the winning claim based on clarity, accuracy, and how well a newcomer would understand the project afterward. The full reward goes to one winner.

This is not financial advice. Do your own research.

claims.title: @ariasnico - $OFFR explained in 7 posts: offline 35B, citations, and the limits (bounty #1525)
claims.description:
X handle: @ariasnico
Thread: https://x.com/ariasnico/status/2118265607284314587 (7 posts, opens by quoting the launch post by @RealShark77)

PROOF IMAGE: the first post of the thread as published, with the quote card and the first replies visible, next to a line-by-line map of the 7 posts and the requirement checklist.
REPO with the thread text, the proof image and its generator: https://github.com/nicoarias81/poidh1525-offr-thread

WHAT THE THREAD DOES
Post 1 leads with the thing that is actually unusual, not the parameter count: the app has no network permission at all. 35B parameters, no wifi, no cloud, no API, cited answers from a library on the phone. It quotes the launch tweet and discloses the bounty.
Post 2 sets the contrast that makes the point land: every other "AI on your phone" is a thin client against a datacenter, and airplane mode is where that breaks - blackout, mountain, hospital basement, throttled network.
Post 3 is the mechanism in three steps: Qwen3-1.7B turns the question into search queries, SQLite full-text search pulls passages from a 24.6 GB library, a bigger model writes the answer with [1]-style citations that open the source.
Post 4 is the hardware story: two models picked by the phone's RAM (4B under 10 GB; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 2 bits streamed from storage from 10 GB, because it is bigger than memory), and the APK has no INTERNET permission - checked in CI - and no Play Services.
Post 5 is the numbers with the repo's own caveats: 54% of Claude Opus 5.5 with web search on 61 blind-graded questions, 4B at 34% on the same set, and the measured latency on an 8 GB Redmi 12 5G (136s to first word, 179s done; 35B there 247s and 507s, unusable).
Post 6 is the part most threads would cut: no 12 GB phone measured, the 54% only 4 points over a 50% bar, the held-out 40-question set never run, answers truncated at the length limit, some restaurant answers refusing to name places.
Post 7 says who it is for (no-SIM travel, first aid in a blackout, field work, asking what you don't want logged) and who it is not (live prices, today's news: a library, not the internet), with the repo and the Base CA 0xee9069e8f520652e59674fad2120f6dea2671ba3.

ACCURACY NOTES
Every number comes from the project's own published benchmarks and its APK manifest; nothing was measured on my own devices, and the thread says so rather than implying first-hand testing. No price talk, no return promises, no comparative claim beyond the 54% the repo publishes. Original writing, no bot spam.

claims.title: 7-post X thread explaining OFFR (Offline Research): how it works, who it's for, honest limits
claims.description:
X thread (7 posts, quotes @RealShark77's announcement): https://x.com/lupilupipuli/status/2117299554135736532
X handle: @lupilupipuli

What the thread covers, in plain words:
1. What OFFR is: an Android app that answers research questions with zero internet, searching a library on the phone and citing the passages it used.
2. How it works: Qwen3-1.7B turns the question into searches; SQLite full-text search over a 24.6 GB on-phone library (Wikipedia most-viewed 31%, Wikivoyage, places by city, first aid, travel facts, Ethereum texts).
3. Answer models: Qwen3-4B under 10 GB RAM; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 2 bits from 10 GB, streamed from storage; tap-able [1] citations.
4. Offline by design: no network permission (checked every build), no Play Services, exact arithmetic for conversions, unsourced parts labelled.
5. Who it's for, plus the MIT repo link.
6. Honest limits from the repo's own logs: 54% vs a frontier AI with web search on 61 tuning questions (graders vary ~10 pts), 40 held-out questions not yet run, only tested on an 8 GB phone (~3 min per answer 4B, ~8.5 min 35B), 29-39 GB storage.
7. @OFFR54, @RealShark77, the Base CA 0xee9069e8f520652e59674fad2120f6dea2671ba3, and the bounty disclosure (#bounty). No price talk, no claims of beating other models.

Every figure is from https://github.com/SharkCube99/offline-research-android (README + docs). Thread text: https://github.com/qlufiq-collab/bounty-submissions/tree/main/poidh-1525-offr-thread
